speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: asked the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth how does the People's Association ensure that stall rentals at trade fairs and bazaars that it manages remain affordable to stallholders.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This is done through the terms of an open tender, which include ensuring the adequate supply of utilities and amenities and the provision of suitable logistical support.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: A successful tenderer will have to comply with the terms of the tender.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: An entity or individual who intends to bid for a stall will know in advance the rental rates which are proposed to be charged as well as the other details on which the trade fair or bazaar is operated.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They can then assess for themselves whether to make a bid.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In the case of the ongoing Bazaar Raya Geylang Serai and Hari Raya Light Up, which I will call "the bazaar", organised by PA since 2014, the above framework that I have just set out would apply.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: There were several bids for the operator and the tender was then awarded to a consortium of operators.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In considering the tender, price is one factor, amongst others.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In the case of the bazaar, the award did not go to the bidder with the highest price.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Since 2019, Wisma Geylang Serai has taken over the organising of the bazaar and is responsible for the overall place-making and programming at the bazaar, which has traditionally been held in the month of Ramadan, leading up to Hari Raya.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Wisma Geylang Serai curates the programming at the precinct, including the bazaar.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The curation of the programming includes the Light Up, concerts, cooking and talk shows and other programmes – all of which add buzz and festivity to the occasion.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It also generates additional footfall to the bazaar.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In addition, the Singapore Tourism Board also promotes the bazaar as a destination for locals and tourists.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This year's bazaar, at 36 days, is the longest festive bazaar on record.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In total, almost 700 stalls were taken up.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Of this, a substantial number of stallholders had previously either operated a stall at the bazaar in a previous year or at some other trade fairs organised by PA or the merchants' association.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: A fair number of the stalls at this year's bazaar also took up more than one stall at the bazaar.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: The Geylang Serai bazaar has gained great public interest and attention.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: There were two different reports mentioning two different things regarding the affordability of the rent.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: One reported that some business owners claimed that by the end of the second or third week of operating, they were already speculating that they may not be able to earn a profit or recover their business costs; whereas the other reported the opposite.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: In view of this, I just want to know whether PA would consider conducting a survey or study to find out: (a) how many businesses face losses and also the range of losses, (b) the number of businesses breaking even, (c) the number of businesses that make profit.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: And more importantly, to make the findings public so as to provide a proper closure in addressing the public concerns on this issue.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, this is the market price that is reflected in an open tender.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Parties come in, they decide what the market price would be and they make a bid for that.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In particular, for a bazaar the size and scale of Geylang Serai, which is not just the bazaar itself but in conjunction with the festive occasion, the Ramadan Light Up and so on, it is important to get the programming, as well as the way in which the bazaar will be operated in a safe way, for both the stall holders as well as the patrons.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: That is why we looked for a professional operator as well as one who has the experience and ability to provide the environment.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, no bidder comes in without knowing what the rates would be and that is an important consideration.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: They have to make their own calculations, that is why I mentioned the market price.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, the bidder knows in advance what the price would be and then they decide.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Others, perhaps, might take a longer period of time.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It is really a question of which stalls, what their offerings are, how popular they might be and so on.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In any typical bazaar or market, there will always be a variety, and there will always be a differential in terms of the takings of the stalls that are there.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I think you cannot expect all to make money and all to be at the same level of profit-taking.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But the point to be made is that they know in advance what the cost would be.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The other point which I made in my answer earlier is that a fair number of these are not inexperienced stallholders.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: They have come from previous trade fairs and other bazaars.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In fact, a fair number, quite a substantial number, not only came from previous years' Geylang Serai bazaar – so they know what it would be like	– but they also came and made bids for multiple stalls in this bazaar.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Again, that is something they have to factor into their own consideration when it comes to market price, what they think they can afford, what they think they can sell and whether they can realise and recoup.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For Wisma Geylang Serai, which operates the entire event, their role, of course, encompasses the bazaar and that is in the hands of the professional operator.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But in addition to that, whatever is tendered, a substantial amount then goes back into the Light Up, the organisation of the event itself and ensuring that the programming, which I had mentioned earlier, drives footfall to the event, and also ensures that the festive occasion is celebrated appropriately, which is PA's and Wisma Geylang Serai's main agenda.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: When you look at that collectively, that is the way in which this bazaar had been run previously, and had been run this year too.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Of course, we will continue to take soundings from not just the stall operators but also the consortium operator, the patrons and people who deal with the security and other aspects of this bazaar, to learn from it so that in subsequent years, it will be better.
